- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the following 5-day horizon.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 3–7% for the next 3–7 days.
- Model frequently fails to capture mean reversion in 10–14 day horizons; if price deviates >10% from 30-day moving average, apply a correction toward the average.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00), model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for the next 5–7 days.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to overestimate if sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply a 3–5% downward bias if sentiment variance >0.4 over last 7 days.
